data.name: Bheesham
data.gender_notes: Bheesham is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: In Hindu mythology, Bheesham is the god of calamity, misfortune, and affliction. He is also known as Shani, the lord of Saturday and the son of Surya, the sun god. Bheesham is believed to test individuals' resolve and discipline, and those who please him are rewarded with prosperity and success. The name Bheesham carries the meaning “God of Calamity” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Bheesham usually hope their child will grow to embody god of calamity and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes the power of adversity to shape character and bring growth.
data.etymology: Bheesham belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “God of Calamity.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Bheesham total 7, giving a life-path number of 7. Number 7 is linked with Ketu and with the qualities of reflection, wisdom and inner depth.

data.cultural_impact: Bheesham is an important deity in Hindu mythology, and his name evokes a deep sense of reverence and awe. He is mentioned in numerous Hindu scriptures and Puranas, and he plays a significant role in various mythological stories. Worship of Bheesham is particularly popular in India and Nepal, where he is believed to bring both suffering and blessings. People observe various rituals and practices to appease him, and they often seek his blessings before embarking on important endeavors.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, Bheesham is seen as a teacher who tests individuals' resolve and discipline. He forces individuals to confront their weaknesses and impurities, and helps them purify their souls. He is also believed to grant boons to those who have true devotion and faith in him. The worship of Bheesham is therefore seen as a means of spiritual growth and self-realization. It is a reminder that even in the face of adversity and suffering, one can find strength and inner peace.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Bheesham symbolizes the embodiment of righteous anger and justice, as portrayed in the epic Mahabharata, where he is the charioteer of Bhishma Pitamaha, the grandsire of the Pandavas. His name signifies the ability to harness anger for righteous purposes, and to stand firm in dharma.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Bheeshma was a great warrior and the grandsire of the Pandavas in Mahabharata. The name Bheesham carried significant spiritual weight in that era.
historical_references.context: Mahabharata is an epic Sanskrit poem that narrates the Kurukshetra War between the Pandava and Kaurava princes.
